chapter: Learning, lawn parties and band rivalries
title: His mother bought him a one-dollar guitar and he taught himself
summary: Dawson tells how his mother bought an old guitar for a dollar from a player and he learned to tune and play it himself.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Oh, you never did tell us about that old man who you started to tell us. He had a guitar, the first guitar you ever saw him, patched up.

And that started me to play. You see, I took my mama, bought the guitar for me for one dollar. She said, my son likes music. I think he's going to make good because he's interested in music. So she said, someday I'm going to get him a guitar and let him work out on it. So he said, well, he can have this old, I'll let him have this old guitar here for one dollar. So she said, well, alright. She had the dollar and she gave him the dollar and he gave her the guitar. When they finished playing they left to the next door from the way they was playing and gave my mama the old guitar and she brought and gave it to me. So, it got out of tune but I didn't know I was just fooling around there with it, you know. Winding up the strings until finally I got to hear him play. It sounds so much like the way it was before and from that on I learned how to tune the guitar up myself.
And nobody helped you at all?

And I took that guitar man and I walked the door. I learned myself. That's how I learned. You didn't watch anybody or anything? I used to watch them go around different places and see fellas playing, you know. I had to cook, good eye, you know. And I'd catch on like that and that's where I went right on up learning how to load all the strings on the guitar and know the name of them and everything. But I break a string and I could go buy the new string and put it on there. And from that on I got so I started playing, picking the guitar. And I just got good then.
